claim: For all integer partitions lam, mu, nu with |lam| = |mu| + |nu| and c^{lam}_{mu nu} > 0, every coefficient of the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} in the monomial basis is nonnegative (the King-Tollu-Toumazet positivity conjecture, 2004).

quadruple.statement: For all integer partitions lam, mu, nu with |lam| = |mu| + |nu| and c^{lam}_{mu nu} > 0, every coefficient of the stretched Littlewood-Richardson polynomial P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} in the monomial basis is nonnegative (the King-Tollu-Toumazet positivity conjecture, 2004).
quadruple.stage: Ehrhart theory of the Knutson-Tao hive polytopes H(lam, mu, nu) in R^{(n-1)(n-2)/2}, n the number of parts, with the rhombus inequalities (0/+-1 normals) as facets; P is the Ehrhart polynomial of H, its coefficients are piecewise polynomial in (lam, mu, nu) on the chambers of the Littlewood-Richardson chamber complex (Rassart 2004), a_k homogeneous of degree k, so a_1 is piecewise linear

shape.objects: Triples (lam, mu, nu) of integer partitions with |lam| = |mu| + |nu| and c > 0: an infinite set, graded by the number of parts n and the size |lam|. For each triple: the integer-valued polynomial P of degree dim H <= (n-1)(n-2)/2 and the rational polytope H (vertex denominators 1 for n <= 4; up to 7 observed at n = 5 and at n = 7 in the box). The Littlewood-Richardson coefficient is not defined in Mathlib (GitHub code search 2026-09-03).
shape.quantifiers: Universal over the infinite set of triples, then universal over the coefficient index: for all (lam, mu, nu), for all k, a_k >= 0. The negative side is one object: a triple with one negative coefficient. Per triple, a decision with a finite exact answer.
shape.target_quantity: A decision: true (a proof for every triple) or false (one exhibited triple with a certified negative coefficient). No constant, exponent, density, or threshold.
shape.ambient_structure: Three kinds of structure coexist: (i) representation theory / symmetric functions (c = multiplicity of s_lam in s_mu s_nu, the lattice-word rule); (ii) polyhedral geometry (c = number of lattice points of the hive polytope; P its Ehrhart polynomial; the Berline-Vergne local formula writes a_k as a sum over k-faces of face volume times a weight of the transverse cone); (iii) the Horn/LR cone and its chamber complex (Rassart: coefficients piecewise polynomial in (lam, mu, nu); KTT 2009: a saturated essential Horn inequality factorises P = P1 P2 into triples with fewer parts). The simpler ambient keeping the constraint: Ehrhart theory of rational polytopes with facet normals in the finite rhombus-normal set N_n (Ferudun 2026).
shape.symmetries: c^{lam}_{mu nu} = c^{lam}_{nu mu}; column addition c^{lam+(1^n)}_{mu+(1^n),nu} = c^{lam}_{mu nu} for n >= max length; both keep P. Conjugation keeps c but not P (stretching does not commute with conjugation). Complementation in a rectangle (the S_3 symmetry of the triple multiplicity) keeps P but changes sizes. The rhombus-normal set is invariant under the dihedral symmetry of the hive triangle. Scaling (lam, mu, nu) -> s(lam, mu, nu) sends P(t) to P(st), so a_k scales by s^k: within a chamber a_1 is linear and homogeneous.
shape.configuration: The forbidden configuration (for the claim) is a sign: a_k < 0 for some k. Algebraic relations: a_0 = 1; D! a_D = normalized volume > 0; a_{D-1} = half the normalized boundary volume > 0; for a full-dimensional hive the coefficients of t^D..t^{D-3} are positive (Ferudun 2026, Thm 2); for a full-dimensional 5-part hive (D = 6) every coefficient but a_1 is positive (Thm 3). In the h*-basis a_1 = H_D + sum_i (-1)^{i-1} h*_i/(i C(D,i)): a negative a_1 needs h*-mass at even or high indices against small h*_1 and small odd entries. The configuration is destroyed by Horn-facet factorisation (a product of coefficientwise-positive polynomials is positive), so a counterexample is primitive or has a primitive counterexample factor.
shape.extremal_candidate: Not applicable (no extremum). Within the box (length <= 7, size <= 30) the structures nearest to negativity are the empty non-unimodular hive simplices of normalized volume 2 (h* = (1, 0, 1, 0, ...), c = D + 1, dimensions 4, 5, 6), whose linear coefficient H_D - 1/(D(D-1)) is the smallest coefficient ratio to the unimodular simplex found: 24/25. Named candidate classes in print: the Chen-Robbins-Yuen case (mu = nu = staircase, lam = 2 staircase), the 3 x N transportation transfer (family positive in the measured range).
shape.finite_certificates: The false side has a finite certificate: one triple with its polynomial (D + 1 exact lattice-point counts, or Normaliz's Ehrhart series) and an index k with a_k < 0, re-checkable by lrcalc and the lattice-word counter. The true side has no finite certificate: a proof for all triples needs an argument (the frontier is the effectivity statement (HTE) of Ferudun 2026); its finite pieces (boxes) are computations of the false side's non-existence in a range.
shape.monotonicity: No monotonicity of the claim in a parameter. The searched region is monotone: settled boxes grow with the number of parts n and the size bound N; a counterexample, if any, lies outside every settled box. Settled: length <= 4 (theorem); length <= 7 and size <= 30 (this project's box attack: 5 parts certified by two implementations, 6 and 7 parts as Normaliz evidence with sampled checks); c <= 2 (theorem). Smallest open instances: 5 parts at size 31, 8 parts at any size.
shape.uniformity_parameter: The number of parts n: the hive dimension (n-1)(n-2)/2 and the cost of one exact polynomial grow with n; the chamber complex grows with n; at n = 5 only a_1 of full-dimensional hives is open, at n >= 6 every coefficient below the top four is open. The size |lam| is a second parameter: within a chamber a_1 is linear in the size, so a chamber where a_1 is negative contains counterexamples of every size, and its smallest integer point may exceed any given box.
shape.proof_shape: For the false side: a search over triples with an exact polynomial per instance (the finite computation of the box attack), guided by the h*-expansion of a_1 and by the piecewise linearity of a_1 (descent along a_1 inside chambers; sampling of chambers unreachable at small sizes), plus transfers of known non-Ehrhart-positive polytopes into hive or LR polytopes (the strip construction realises k x N transportation polytopes as LR polytopes). For the true side: the Berline-Vergne local formula on period-one hive polytopes reduces the conjecture to the effectivity statement (HTE); termwise positivity fails at codimension 4, so a proof must control closed coarsenings globally (Ferudun 2026); no argument reaching the statement is recorded.
shape.neighbours: (1) Positivity for length <= 4: known true (Ferudun 2026). (2) c = 1 => P = 1 and c = 2 => P = t + 1: known true. (3) Polynomiality: known true (Derksen-Weyman; Rassart; Thawinrak). (4) Top four coefficients of full-dimensional hives positive; five-part full-dimensional hives positive except possibly a_1: known true (Ferudun 2026). (5) Positivity inside the box length <= 7, size <= 30: known true by computation (this project: 5 parts proved by two independent implementations; 6 and 7 parts evidence), sibling workspace attack/stretched-lr-polynomial-negative-coefficient. (6) Ehrhart positivity of general lattice polytopes: known false (Reeve simplices; smooth examples of Castillo et al. 2018; order polytopes from dimension 14, Liu-Tsuchiya 2019, Liu-Xin-Zhang 2026). (7) Skew Gelfand-Tsetlin and marked order polytopes (stretched Kostka): Ehrhart positive (Jochemko-Menon 2026). (8) The 3 x 8 transportation family (dimension 14, codegree 3): Ehrhart positive in the measured range (ktt-positivity repository). (9) Stretched Newell-Littlewood coefficients: quasi-polynomial, positivity conjectured (King 2021): open. (10) The Epoch FrontierMath open problem: the same claim's negation inside the box, now decided negative by computation.
shape.known_bounds: Positive side: length <= 4 (theorem); c <= 2 (theorem); full-dimensional 5-part hives, a_2..a_6 (theorem); the box length <= 7, size <= 30 (computation, 6.8 million polynomials, none negative; every 5-part polynomial pinned by lrcalc); 'extensive computation' and a ~4 x 10^8-triple search with no hit (Ferudun 2026, ranges unrecorded); the 3 x 8 transportation family positive with minimum linear coefficient 2157/280. Negative side: none. Documented ceilings: termwise Berline-Vergne positivity fails at codimension 4 (a cell of weight -349/28800) and (HTE) is unproved; the box attack found the minimal coefficient ratio 24/25 (volume-2 empty simplices) and minimal a_1 exactly H_D otherwise, so nothing in the box leans toward negativity; exhaustive enumeration beyond the box costs a factor of about 1.8 per unit of size and the polynomials of 8-part hives cost seconds each.
shape.missing_input: For the negative side: a triple, or a chamber of the LR chamber complex on which the linear form a_1 (or a higher coefficient's polynomial) takes a negative value; no argument in print locates one, and the box attack shows the nearest structures (volume-2 empty simplices) are far from it. For the positive side: (HTE) of Ferudun 2026.
shape.base_theory: ZFC. Every instance is a finite integer computation (lattice-point counts of a rational polytope, exact interpolation), provable in Peano arithmetic; the positive side's known partial proofs (Ferudun 2026) use the Berline-Vergne local formula and exact rational computation, inside ZFC; no hypothesis beyond ZFC bears on the claim or on any neighbour. No Mathlib definition of the objects (2026-09-03).

known: The box result of the sibling attack (attack/stretched-lr-polynomial-negative-coefficient, 2026-09-03/04): no partitions of length <= 7 and size <= 30 give a negative coefficient; the 5-part part is certified by lrcalc and Normaliz agreeing on all 1,334,669 polynomials; the 6- and 7-part parts rest on Normaliz with sampled independent recounts (4,217,762 and 1,302,871 polynomials, plus 9,201,781 7-part triples reduced by the KTT factorisation theorem).

P(t) = c^{t lam}_{t mu, t nu} is a polynomial in t: Derksen and Weyman, J. Algebra 255 (2002) 247-257; Rassart, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 107 (2004) 161-179 (piecewise polynomiality in (lam, mu, nu) on a chamber complex); Thawinrak, arXiv:2211.06810.
c = number of integer hives (lattice points of the hive polytope), saturation: Knutson and Tao, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999) 1055-1090.

The positivity conjecture, the hive model, degree bound deg P <= d(G), linear factors (t+1)...(t+M): King, Tollu, Toumazet, CRM Proc. Lecture Notes 34 (2004) 99-112; Sem. Lothar. Combin. 54A (2006) B54Ad.

Factorisation: a saturated essential Horn inequality (I, J, K) in R^n_r gives c = c1 c2 and P = P1 P2 for the triples (lam_K, mu_I, nu_J) and the complements: King, Tollu, Toumazet, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 116 (2009) 314-333, doi:10.1016/j.jcta.2008.06.005; stated as Theorem 1.3 in Cho, Jung, Moon, DMTCS proc. AJ (2008) 483-494, doi:10.46298/dmtcs.3592 (read in full). The essential triple counts are 12, 41, 142, 521, 2042 for n = 3..7 (this project, lrcalc).

c = 1 => P = 1: Knutson, Tao, Woodward, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (2004) 19-48. c = 2 => P = t + 1: Ikenmeyer, J. Algebraic Combin. 44 (2016) 1-29; Sherman, J. Algebra (2017), doi:10.1016/j.jalgebra.2017.03.011.
